sources.title: Palworld Server Guide - RCON ("RCON is now deprecated. Please consider to use REST API.")
Palworld Server Guide - REST API: Get player list (name, accountName, playerId, userId...)
Palworld Server Guide - REST API: Kick player (body field "userid")
palworld-server-tool api/player.go - getPlayerActionUserId() returns steam_<SteamId> for kick/ban/unban
pal_rcon models.py - skips the literal header "name,playeruid,steamid"; kickplayer/banplayer take a bare steam id
PalworldServerTools.ps1 - sends "KickPlayer <steamid>", matches "failed to kick"/"failed to ban", appends "steam_<steamid>" to banlist.txt
palworld-server-player-logger - live ShowPlayers sample: playeruid 1166585980, steamid 76561198035441627
XGamingServer docs - "/KickPlayer steam_76561198012345678"; Xbox/PS5 use their platform UserID
SurvivalServers wiki (edited 31 Aug 2026) - "...use that longer form in REST calls, and the plain number in chat commands"
BattleMetrics Palworld RCON - broadcast is cut off at the first space; spaces replaced with underscores

notes:
IDENTIFIER (printed vs accepted): PRINTED - ShowPlayers answers with a CSV block. The header line is literally "name,playeruid,steamid" (Charahiro/pal_rcon's models.py skips that exact string: `if line == "name,playeruid,steamid": continue`) and a row looks like "Rcat999,1166585980,76561198035441627" - name, then a DECIMAL playeruid, then the Steam id. rinjugatla/palworld-server-player-logger publishes a live sample with playeruid "1166585980" / steamid "76561198035441627" / playeruid_hex "4588b07c"; the playeruid is the decimal value of the first 8 hex characters of the REST API's playerId field (zaigie/palworld-server-tool getPlayerUid()). A player who is still loading or in character creation prints playeruid "00000000" instead. On crossplay servers the third column is reported as a PLATFORM-PREFIXED user id, not a bare number: thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker documents the row shape in scripts/player_logging.sh as "<name>,<player_id>,(steam|ps5|gdk)_<id>". ACCEPTED - NOT SETTLED, and the sources genuinely conflict. Pocketpair's own command page (docs version 1.0.4) still says "/KickPlayer <SteamID>" with no prefix, and Charahiro/pal_rcon sends "kickplayer <17-digit steamid>"; but the REST API that Pocketpair now directs admins to takes {"userid": "steam_7656..."}, banlist.txt stores entries as "steam_7656..." (shupershuff/PalworldServerTools writes exactly "steam_$steamid"), and two independent hosting docs publish the prefixed form for RCON too (GGServers 2025-05-09: "KickPlayer steam_<Steam ID here>"; XGamingServer: "/KickPlayer steam_76561198012345678" plus "For Xbox/PS5 crossplay players, use their platform UserID instead of steam_"). This file therefore emits the PREFIXED form via playerId.prefix "steam_" - it is the only form that can also name an Xbox (gdk_) or PS5 (ps5_) player - but the bare form is a live alternative, see CANDIDATES. Because playerId.prefix is stripped on input, the CSV parse works whether the third column prints "76561198035441627" or "steam_76561198035441627". A wrong form is NOT silent: the server's reply contains "failed to kick" / "failed to ban" (shupershuff/PalworldServerTools matches exactly those strings on the RCON response), so a runtime can detect rejection and try the next candidate.

CANDIDATES: kick / ban / unban argument, most likely first. (1) "steam_76561198035441627" - the platform UserId form. Sources: Palworld REST API kick/ban/unban userid field (official docs); zaigie/palworld-server-tool api/player.go getPlayerActionUserId(), whose comment reads "prefer the full UserId (supports cross-platform), fall back to steam_ + SteamId"; banlist.txt line format; GGServers 2025-05-09; XGamingServer. (2) "76561198035441627" - bare SteamID64. Sources: official command page v1.0.4 "/KickPlayer <SteamID>"; survivalservers wiki last edited 31 Aug 2026 - "The REST API lists the same players with the ID in the form steam_<SteamID64> - use that longer form in REST calls, and the plain number in chat commands"; Charahiro/pal_rcon; shupershuff/PalworldServerTools sends "KickPlayer <bare steamid>". (3) the decimal playeruid from column 2, e.g. "1166585980" - DavidJS01/palcon documents kick as "Kick a player given a Palworld UID or Steam ID", and valamidev/palworld-rcon-buddy's README example is {"command":"KickPlayer 41XXXXX2"}, which is a playeruid, not a SteamID64.

RCON IS DEPRECATED BY THE PUBLISHER. docs.palworldgame.com/api/rcon now carries only: "RCON is now deprecated. Please consider to use REST API." RCON still exists and is still what panels drive (BattleMetrics ships a Palworld RCON tool; thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker still ships rcon-cli), so transport is recorded as rcon - but the publisher-sanctioned channel is now the REST API on RESTAPIPort (RESTAPIEnabled), basic auth as user "admin" with AdminPassword, base path /v1/api: GET /v1/api/info, GET /v1/api/players (fields name, accountName, playerId, userId, ip, ping, location_x, location_y, level, building_count), POST /v1/api/kick {"userid":...}, /v1/api/ban, /v1/api/unban, /v1/api/announce {"message":...}. zaigie/palworld-server-tool has already moved kick/ban/unban/showplayers/broadcast off RCON onto those REST endpoints, and Charahiro/pal_rcon's README now says RCON looks abandoned and points at its own REST client. If RCON stops answering, this file should be re-cut as transport "rest".

COMMANDS ARE SENT WITHOUT A LEADING SLASH over RCON. The slash form (/KickPlayer ...) is the in-game chat form. Confirmed in code: palworld-server-docker runs `rcon-cli "Broadcast Hello everyone"`, zaigie/palworld-server-tool sends "Info", Charahiro/pal_rcon sends "kickplayer"/"showplayers" lowercase, shupershuff sends "KickPlayer $steamid". Command names are case-insensitive; the casing here is Pocketpair's.

BROADCAST IS TRUNCATED AT THE FIRST SPACE. BattleMetrics' Palworld RCON page: "The game currently cuts off any messages sent at the first space. To work around this problem we automatically replace spaces with underscores." A caller that needs multi-word broadcasts over RCON must substitute underscores for spaces itself, or use POST /v1/api/announce, which does not have this bug. Palworld RCON is also ASCII-only: Charahiro/pal_rcon encodes outbound payloads as ASCII because UTF-8 corrupts both the request and the response, and Lukium/palworld-admin reports that a single player with a non-ASCII name breaks the whole ShowPlayers reply and makes kick/ban fail. zaigie/palworld-server-tool has an opt-in base64 RCON mode for this.

BAN ONLY REACHES ONLINE PLAYERS. shupershuff/PalworldServerTools falls back to appending "steam_<steamid>\n" to Pal/Saved/SaveGames/banlist.txt when the target is offline, with the comment "ARRCON can only ban players who are online". Hence banList. BanPlayer takes no reason and no duration - bans are permanent until the id is removed from banlist.txt or UnBanPlayer is run. UnBanPlayer is in Pocketpair's command table for v1.0.4, but Nodecraft's page (updated 07/01/26) still says "there is no unban command" and tells admins to edit banlist.txt; treat the file as the reliable path and the command as the fast path. There is no MOTD command, so motd is omitted. ShowPlayers responses are also flaky: pal_rcon retries ShowPlayers up to 10 times by default because the reply frequently arrives truncated.

CONFIDENCE is low and the reason is the identifier, not the command names: the command names (Info, ShowPlayers, KickPlayer, BanPlayer, UnBanPlayer, Broadcast) are agreed by every source including Pocketpair, but no source I could reach shows the exact accepted argument working on a current (crossplay-era) server, and the two best-dated sources contradict each other. Nothing here has been run against a live server.
